Resolves #20562

Adds part 2 of *How an AI team remembers*: `learn/blog/context-compaction-recovery-for-ai-coding-agents.md`, led by the search term `context compaction recovery` (#20278 map, Julia's term read). It covers one agent's recovery after compaction, kept inside the series frame. The recovery runbook is shown as a team artifact. Its steps came from five maintainers across four model families (GPT, Claude, Kimi, Gemini), each step linked to the ticket and PR of the failure that produced it. The ordinary case is a real recovery from 7 November with public receipts (#20514, #20521, #20522). It sits beside the `MemoryCore.md` war story, and "Where it falls short" includes the skipped direction check and "a recovered task is not a recovered purpose". The post is registered in `blog.json` as part 2 of 8, and part 1's series list now links it.

Evidence: L1 (prose + portal render) → L1 required (docs; AC-6's static URL is post-merge). agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The preview challenge (operator, after opening).** A cold reader who sees only the title and subtitle would skip the first version: "the record" is our jargon, there was no "AI coding agent" in it, and nothing promised a usable checklist.
  - New title: "Context compaction recovery for AI coding agents: six checks, not a summary". It carries the primary term and the audience.
  - The subtitle is cut to one pain and one payoff.
  - The post opens with the August incident from #16618 as a scene instead of an abstract thesis. That incident is a deliberation the agent said was never saved, which sat unopened in its own handover.
  - Two H2s carry search terms: "Why the compaction summary is not enough" and "Six checks after a context compaction".
  - The opening names the harnesses our maintainers run (Claude Code, Codex).
- **The diagram.** The ticket's single recovery-sequence visual is a grouped flowchart: three question pairs (what changed / what was I doing / is it still true), then the ledger. As a flat chain it rendered 1,558 px tall at 1440 px wide; grouped, it renders 1,063 px.
- **The closing section (operator, after Julia's approval).** "Where it falls short" read as a list of red flags, and two of its claims were never V-B-A'd. The seat already has mechanisms there:
  - SessionStart hooks run at every compaction.
  - A Stop hook enforces the lane state.
  - Wake-ups deliver teammates' messages.

  The section is now "Where the runbook goes next". It frames the next rows of the lineage table:
  - start the six checks from the compaction signal, which is Vega's Option H on #16139;
  - hand every check its inputs up front.

  It cites `seatProjectionCheck.mjs` (`98603a4`, L11: "failed open 319 consecutive times") as the friction→gold precedent. The cost and write-side points become plain facts, no longer framed as warnings. The "recovered task is not a recovered purpose" bullet is dropped: the purpose was in the agent's memory index, so it was never a runbook gap.
- **The cover (operator-approved).** Pages neomjs/pages#66 adds `summary-checks-ledger.png` (2400×1260, part 1's style). It shows the summary, the six checks with their tools, and the ledger, and it is embedded after the byline as part 1 does. **neomjs/pages#66 must merge first**, otherwise the image 404s. The cover doubles as the Medium visual, where the Mermaid block does not render.

The series section opens on where the memory began: one local stdio MCP server registered with Gemini CLI on 2025-10-17 (`ab6186702f`, #7521), whose server still defaults to stdio (`Server.mjs:55` at `cf17e6c`). It ends where it stands today: a team's shared memory in a seven-service compose stack (`b282d7e`), with local models that embed, summarize and digest the sessions into a graph that ranks the next work. There's no market claim, and the post doesn't call stdio an on-ramp, because Brain #699 retired the Fleet's per-seat stdio target.
